title: Nepal Begins Process to Declare 213 Missing Indians Presumed Dead After August Floods
excerpt: Kathmandu has published the missing list from the August 26 Trishuli-Bhotekoshi flash floods. Families of missing Indians have until December 2 to file objections with the Indian Embassy before declarations of death are issued.
body:
• Nepal has begun the legal process to presume and declare dead 213 Indian nationals still missing since the August 26 flash floods in the Trishuli-Bhotekoshi river system.
  • The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) has published a list of 3,915 missing people, including 623 foreign nationals from 19 countries; at least 1,453 people are confirmed dead and more than 5,000 remain missing.
  • Families of missing Indians can file objections or corrections with the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu by December 2, by email at eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or by phone and WhatsApp on +9779851316807.
  • After the comment period closes, Nepal will finalise the list and issue formal declarations of death; the embassy will then obtain death certificates from local authorities in Nepal.

Nepal has begun the process of presuming and formally declaring dead 213 Indian nationals who have been missing since flash floods tore through the Trishuli-Bhotekoshi river system on August 26, the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu said in a press release on Wednesday, November 25.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) has published the list of the missing on its website and invited objections and requests for additions, deletions or corrections. The floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border, killed at least 1,453 people and left more than 5,000 missing, according to the NDRRMA, and damaged physical infrastructure along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, including around a dozen hydropower projects.

The missing, by the numbers

The NDRRMA list contains 3,915 names in total: 3,292 Nepalese nationals and 623 foreign nationals from 19 countries. The authority says it has received verified details of 452 missing foreign nationals through the diplomatic missions of 12 countries. Indians form the largest group, with 213 people, followed by 85 Chinese nationals, 69 Americans, 32 British nationals and 27 Canadians, along with nine Singaporeans, six South Africans, four French nationals, two each from Hungary, Belgium and Kazakhstan, and one Belarusian.

What families need to do

The embassy has asked family members of Indians who remain missing to review the published list and submit any concerns, objections or proposed amendments before December 2. Families can write to eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or call or message +9779851316807. The embassy said additional information and documents might be sought from family members during the process, and that it would provide further updates in the coming days.

"After completing the process of seeking comments/amendments, the Government of Nepal will finalise the list and formally issue the declaration of death."

— Embassy of India, Kathmandu

What happens next

Once the comment period ends, the Nepal government will finalise the list and formally issue the declarations of death. The Indian Embassy will then begin obtaining death certificates for the individuals from the relevant local authorities in Nepal — the documents families typically need to settle insurance, bank accounts, employment benefits and inheritance matters in India. For families of the missing, the December 2 deadline is the immediate step: anyone whose relative's name is missing from the list, or whose details are recorded incorrectly, should contact the embassy before it closes.
